_comment: User-scope MCP templates for `claude mcp add --scope user`; commands, arguments and environment key names follow the selected native sources, with no credentials or host-specific secret values. ${HOME} and ${ECO_ROOT} are repository placeholders: render them for the target host and keep rendered paths out of this template. install_claude_profile.py registers these entries but does not install their upstream packages (adoption/bootstrap.md step 4a). Its Python string.Template pass consumes $$ once; SocratiCode's escaped $${SOCRATICODE_SPEC:-socraticode@latest} therefore reaches Claude as the native ${SOCRATICODE_SPEC:-socraticode@latest} argument. Do not pre-render that token in the client-config map. Claude's v1.16.0 vendor plugin selects .claude-plugin/mcp.json, whose command is bare npx -y --prefer-online with the same native argument. adoption/templates/claude.settings.template.json enables socraticode@socraticode, pins its marketplace to v1.16.0 and sets SOCRATICODE_SPEC to socraticode@1.16.0; the map gates all three settings to the code-search owner. A host's existing same-version local-folder Spec remains host-owned. Keep the manual entry's socraticode name and seventeen explicit environment settings: Claude 2.1.295 expands both registrations before suppressing the matching plugin server (docs/decisions/2026-10-08-claude-mcp-template-alignment.md). Codex retains its independent platform pin and Node launch; parity tests compare the shared backend environment and permit these documented client launch differences. Serena uses its native console script in the claude-code context; the bootstrap uv-tool layout places it in ${ECO_ROOT}/bin. The ai-memory URL and SocratiCode endpoints are repository defaults; the new-WSL map supplies the selected host's endpoints. The profile installer compares environment key names and preserves an existing matching registration's host values. `claude mcp add` refuses an existing name; --replace-mcp re-registers every differing entry, including ai-memory. A selective replacement removes only the intended names at user scope before the profile's --only mcp pass. jcodemunch is user-scoped under the 2026-10-04 decision; the profile neither runs jcodemunch-mcp init nor removes project-local registrations. context-mode supplies its server through its plugin. Claude uses the global MCP_TIMEOUT rather than Codex's per-server startup timeouts. headroom carries its documented offline variables; qmd uses the shared HTTP catalog service. The codebase-memory-mcp registration follows DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp v0.11.0's manual form: a bare frontend binary with no arguments. The vendor's native installer owns its installation and native client edits; this profile projects the selected registration without invoking that installer. Each frontend shares a per-account daemon, so the entry is not wrapped in a bounded runner whose cgroup cleanup could also stop that daemon. Registration, component slot ownership and agent tool permissions remain distinct; the map's code-graph owner is codebase-memory.
